source_locator: R2225: ch. VI; R2226: the October battles
notes: Miller, chapter VI, and Zimmerman: the 2nd Division’s October counter-offensive, 23–26 October 1942. Miller names the 4th, 16th and 29th Infantry among the regiments whose combat strength was reduced; Colonels Furumiya (29th) and Toshiro Hiroyasu (16th) were among the dead. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: south of Bloody Ridge and the Lunga perimeter, second night of the inland assault
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (the 16th and 29th Regiments pressed their attacks until daylight on 26 October); R2228: C25080233000 p. 28 (stamp 0578), the left wing on the night of the 25th was reinforced with the 16th Infantry, and part of the regiment was stopped by wire and did not succeed by dawn
current_activity: attacking the southern perimeter on the second night
engaged_note: 164th Infantry, with the 1st Battalion, 7th Marines (Miller, ch. VI)
notes: Miller, chapter VI: after the 29th Infantry’s assault of the night of 24–25 October, the 16th and 29th Regiments pressed attacks until daylight on 26 October. The 16th had been in reserve on the first night. The claim date is 25 October, the evening the second night’s attacks began. Confidence 0.5. Confidence is raised from 0.5 to 0.7. The 17th Army operations record (JACAR C25080233000, stamp 0578) independently confirms that the 16th Infantry took part in the left-wing night assault of 25 October, which agrees with Miller, chapter VI (the 16th and 29th pressed the inland attacks that night).
